rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for RNA-only models. This tests the simplest configuration (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) to measure baseline performance, which will inform comparisons with more complex multimodal setups later. It clarifies the impact of using RNA data alone and avoids premature exploration of unproven combinations.

The existing evidence shows that the RNA-only singleprofile model (config_001) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. The next experiment tests whether using multiprofile with average pooling aggregation (config_002) improves performance, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. This balances exploration of key design choices (multiprofile vs. singleprofile) while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder consistent, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile ones. This experiment tests the impact of switching RNA encoders from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool aggregation. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, to determine if improving this component can further boost performance beyond the current best of 0.5907.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method to transformer (while keeping rna_encoder=scvi_n200 and multiprofile) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation strategy, a key design choice, and builds on the promising direction of scvi_n200 in multiprofile settings.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only with multiprofile, scvi_n200, and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt while maintaining multiprofile and transformer aggregation could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, which is critical for determining if more advanced encoders (like scgpt) outperform existing ones (scvi_n200) in this setting.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting achieve the highest accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests combining this strong RNA encoder with image data (resnet50) using avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, which directly addresses whether multimodal approaches can improve performance. It isolates the effect of adding image modality while building on the best RNA-only configuration, balancing exploitation of current leads with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests adding multimodal data (resnet50 image encoder) with the same RNA encoder and transformer aggregation but weighted fusion, isolating the impact of image data integration. It balances exploitation of the best RNA setup with exploration of multimodal potential, which could yield higher accuracy if image data provides complementary information.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping other components the same, to determine if the stronger image encoder further improves performance. This isolates the effect of the image encoder, a critical design choice, and leverages the strong prior evidence for the other components.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether using scgpt as the RNA encoder (instead of scvi_n200) with the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and fusion strategy could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice on multimodal performance, a critical design choice with limited prior testing.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and transformer aggregation, which could isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice while maintaining high-quality image features. It clarifies whether scgpt's performance with these components rivals scvi_n200, using the last budget to resolve uncertainty about RNA encoder effectiveness in top-tier multimodal setups.
